Subject: Post-call: LumenHealth streaming quality & model fit — next steps

Hi Sophie / Samir — great to meet you both today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: integrate real-time summarization + guided Q&A into clinician-facing dashboard (short prompts, streaming partials visible as tokens arrive).
- Key constraints: HIPAA-sensitive PHI handling, 99.9% availability target for core flows, and 200 RPS burst for peak shift hours.
- Observed pain: when you tried live demo, partial outputs sometimes cut off mid-phrase and stop tokens were inconsistent across test prompts (you flagged both coherence of partials and stop-sequence truncation).

What we propose first (short runway):
1) Baseline eval: run the attached prompt set against 3 candidate model variants to capture token-level coherence and stop-seq behavior. I attached LumenHealth_prompt_set_v1.json.
2) Streaming UX benchmarks: p50/p95 per-token latency and end-to-end first-token time for short responses (<=40 tokens). We'll surface both streaming and aggregated metrics.
3) Security/compliance checklist: we will include SOC2 scope and brief on VPC/private deploy options; Samir — I know you wanted on-prem feasibility notes.

Next steps / asks:
- Sophie: confirm if the prompt set covers the 2 additional clinical templates (SOAP notes + discharge summary) by EOD Wednesday.
- Samir: please share the list of internal reviewers for security/compliance (email addresses) so we can include them on evidence requests.
- Internal (Tessa / Rishi): can you run a quick triage against our small-streaming harness and return a quick model recommendation + short benchmark by Thursday? If possible include a quantized variant to show lower memory and latency.

Attachments: LumenHealth_prompt_set_v1.json (19 KB)

Thanks — I’ll schedule a follow-up template/working session once we have the baseline metrics.

Best,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: LumenHealth streaming quality & model fit — next steps

Quick summary of what I ran and recommendations (results attached as LumenHealth_benchmark_results_v1.csv):

What we tested (small-streaming harness):
- Prompt set: LumenHealth_prompt_set_v1.json (20 prompts, mix of SOAP/discharge/Q&A) - Model variants: 
  1) mistral-instruct-7b-stream-v1 (high-coherence streaming variant)
  2) llama2-13b-chat-q4_0 (quantized, lower memory footprint)
  3) redwood-instruct-3b (baseline cheap fast)

Key measured metrics (short responses <= 40 tokens):
- First-token time (median): mistral-instruct-7b-stream-v1 = 110 ms, llama2-13b-chat-q4_0 = 140 ms, redwood-instruct-3b = 95 ms.
- Token p50/p95 (per-token time): mistral p50=28 ms / p95=120 ms; llama2 p50=35 ms / p95=240 ms; redwood p50=22 ms / p95=160 ms.
- End-to-end median response (<=40 tokens): mistral ~420 ms, llama2-q4 ~560 ms, redwood-instruct-3b ~360 ms.

Observations on coherence & stop-seq behavior:
- mistral-instruct-7b-stream-v1 produced the most coherent partials; partial outputs generally read as complete phrases rather than garbled fragments. Stop-seq handling was better but not perfect when prompts used non-standard punctuation (e.g., lists).
- llama2-13b-chat-q4_0 showed occasional early termination on stop tokens for 3 of the 20 prompts — likely due to tokenizer differences after quantization; recommended mitigation: explicit <EOS> token and adjust stop sequence tokenization (see example below).
- redwood-instruct-3b is fastest but more prone to repetition in partials; acceptable as background batch worker but not ideal for clinician-facing real-time surface.

Recommendations (concise):
1) Primary candidate for clinician UX: mistral-instruct-7b-stream-v1 (best balance of coherent partials and tolerable latency).
2) Secondary (cost-saving) candidate: llama2-13b-chat-q4_0 for background, non-interactive summarization; follow with small post-process step to stitch partials for final output.
3) Stop-sequence mitigations: add explicit EOS token in prompt templates (e.g., "

### END_OF_RESPONSE###") and pass that as stop token to the streaming API; keep stop sequence short and token-aligned. For quantized models, prefer stop sequences that map to single tokens.
4) Prompt-level trick: end prompts with a short deterministic cue (e.g., "TL;DR: 
" or "Summary:") to reduce mid-sentence stops.

Deliverables attached: LumenHealth_benchmark_results_v1.csv (side-by-side partial vs final), short one-page model recommendation (attached inline, also uploaded to drive link).

Timing note: ran initial sweep in ~3 hours; can expand to 100+ prompts for a full eval next week. If Sophie wants, we can also run a small SOC2-compatible evidence package for the VPC/private options.

Let me know if you want me to package these into a short deck for the Thursday check-in.
